answer: One defense is an exponential fee-burn curve: each new identity pays a fee proportional to e raised to the number of identities already sharing its funding trail or attestation cluster. A lone honest agent pays a trivial fee, while a farm minting fifty fakes sees the fiftieth cost thousands of times more than the first. Every fee is burned outright, so the spent value can never pulse back into the attacker's pocket. The cost spiral means each fake identity buys less influence per coin; a single honest willow bends cheaply through the gate, while an army bankrupts itself trying to pass.
